content.coverIntro: Kramer Bouwservice B.V. runs six to seven renovation and new-build projects at the same time, spread across Noord-Brabant and Zeeland. This proposal focuses on one concrete problem: the weekly margin-per-project overview that currently takes three to four hours of manual merging and only shows afterwards whether a project was profitable.
content.situation: Every site foreman records his hours on his own Excel timesheet and emails it to Lisa every week. Lisa manually pastes those timesheets into an overview per project and links the purchase invoices that come in through the accounts by hand. That takes her three to four hours every Monday. The result is lagging by definition: on a project in Bergen op Zoom it only became clear after completion that underestimated material costs had almost wiped out the margin. A month earlier they could still have course-corrected on hours or additional work with the client. An ERP module is not an option: it requires site foremen to type their hours directly into the system, and they are up on the scaffolding, not behind a laptop.
goals: Have an up-to-date margin overview per project every Monday morning before the meeting with Erik, without manual cutting and pasting
Be able to course-correct on margin during a project instead of finding out afterwards that a project was not profitable
Flag projects that drop below 15% margin early
Free up the three to four hours a week now spent on merging for other work
content.approach: We connect Exact Online - which already holds the sales invoices, purchase invoices and time registration - to a Power BI dashboard that automatically calculates the margin per project: revenue minus booked hours and purchases. The site foremen keep working the way they are used to; their Excel timesheets remain the source for hours on site, and Lisa submits them weekly as she does now, but without having to merge anything herself. The dashboard shows the margin per project against one fixed threshold of 15%, and flags projects that drop below it. This way Lisa sees at a glance every Monday morning which projects need attention, before the meeting with Erik starts.
scopeDeliverables: Connection to Exact Online for sales invoices, purchase invoices and time registration per project
Automatic processing of the site foremen's weekly Excel timesheets into hours per project
Power BI dashboard with margin per project (revenue minus booked hours and purchases), with one fixed margin threshold of 15%
Alert flag for projects that drop below the threshold
Weekly automatic refresh, ready before the Monday-morning meeting
Short guide for Lisa on submitting the timesheets weekly so the processing keeps working

phases.name: Week 1: scoping and data connection
phases.description: Set up the Exact Online connection for sales, purchases and hours, align project and cost centre coding, and define the fixed format for the timesheets.

phases.name: Week 2-3: build dashboard
phases.description: Build the Power BI dashboard with margin per project, the fixed 15% threshold, and the alert flag for projects below it.

phases.name: Week 4: test and deliver
phases.description: Run one cycle with real data from running projects, adjust based on feedback from Lisa, and deliver before the next Monday-morning meeting.

content.investment: This project is scoped as one clearly defined problem - the margin-per-project overview - at a fixed price. The investment is expected to fall within the range of a short, clearly defined implementation (indicatively a few thousand euros up to a low five-figure sum), depending on the Exact Online setup and the number of timesheets. We will confirm the exact price after a short scoping call.
content.nextSteps: Approval of this proposal, followed by a short scoping call (about 30 minutes) with Lisa and Erik to go through the Exact Online connection and the timesheet format. After that we start straight away in week 1.
